title: Prescribing rises faster than any death rate
context: In England, the number of people prescribed ADHD drugs has nearly quadrupled since 2016/17, far faster than antidepressants or recorded depression. Prescription records say which medicine was given, never why.
ask: What symptoms and diagnoses sit behind these prescriptions, and who decided a medicine was the answer?

series.label: ADHD drugs
series.about: People in England given at least one prescription for a stimulant or other ADHD medicine (BNF 4.4) in the year, counted once however many items they received.

series.label: Antidepressants
series.about: People given at least one antidepressant (BNF 4.3) in the year. Antidepressants are also prescribed for pain, sleep and anxiety, so this is not a count of people with depression.

series.label: Dementia drugs
series.about: People given at least one drug for dementia (BNF 4.11) in the year. These slow symptoms; they do not stop the disease.

series.label: Antipsychotics
series.about: People given at least one drug used in psychoses and related disorders (BNF 4.2). Most antipsychotic prescribing in England is for conditions other than schizophrenia.

series.label: Sleeping pills and anxiolytics
series.about: People given at least one hypnotic or anxiolytic (BNF 4.1), mostly benzodiazepines and z-drugs. Guidance since the 2010s discourages long-term use.

series.label: Depression diagnoses (GP register)
series.about: Adults on GP practice depression registers: anyone diagnosed since April 2006 whose depression has not been marked resolved. A record of diagnosis, not a count of people currently ill.

numbers.text: people in England on ADHD drugs in 2025/26, from 115,945 in 2016/17.
adults on GP depression registers, 2016/17 to 2024/25 (faint line).

caption: Each line starts at 100 in 2016/17. ADHD drugs are the bold line; the faint line is adults on GP depression registers, on the same index. No register figure was published for 2023/24.

sources.title: Medicines Used in Mental Health, England, 2016/17 to 2025/26

sources.title: Depression: QOF prevalence (18+)

caveats: Prescribing is not prevalence: these lines count people given a medicine, not people who are ill.
Prescription data records the medicine, not the reason it was prescribed.
Community prescribing only: hospitals, prisons and private prescribers are not included.
